[370] Métis and Non Status First Nations
[371] Read pages 135 – 142 and answer the following questions
[374] Why do you think the Federal Government only wanted to deal with individual Métis people as opposed to a collective basis? (1)
[378] In 1934, the Alberta government responded to the pressures of Métis land rights and their request for education, medical care, and free hunting and fishing permits by creating The Ewing Commission.  This commission recommended the creation  of Métis farming  colonies on crown land, under the supervision of the provincial government.  This led to the passage, in 1938, of the Métis population betterment Act. (5)
[382] Which Indigenous groups do the Federal Government claim responsibility for and which do they not?  Why? (2)

[536] Assignment 2.3 Research project: Specific Land Claims /36
[537] Using the internet, this textbook, the library, and any other resources at your disposal, research TWO of the land claims from Alberta listed below.
[539] Lubicon Lake Cree Land Claim
[540] Woodland Cree Settlement
[541] Loon River Settlement
[542] Nakoda (Stoney) Submission
[543] Siksika (Blackfoot) Submission
[544] Blood-Cardston Claim
[545] Peigan Nation Claim
[548] You must include the following elements:
[549] The main events and issues of each claim
[550] Include if, how and when they were settled
[551] If they are not settled, explain why.
[552] A timeline of important events
[553] Explore the benefits, or proposed benefits for the communities involved.
[554] Using a digital platform, explain each claim including graphics such as maps or photos. Should you use a slide presentation, your project summary and comparison of the two claims should be no longer than 12 slides. Share your document with your instructor when it is complete, or print it out and staple it to this page.
